summary: 58-year-old man with prolapsing haemorrhoids needing manual reduction and bright red bleeding, never had a colonoscopy. ASCRS 2024: grade III → rubber band ligation or excisional haemorrhoidectomy; the bleeding must not be attributed to haemorrhoids without colonic evaluation at this age.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Lumps coming down from the back passage with bleeding
inputs.hpi: Two years of lumps prolapsing on straining that he pushes back after each bowel motion, with bright red blood on the paper and in the pan, and mucus soiling. Bowel habit unchanged. No weight loss. Never had a colonoscopy or FIT. No family history.

exam.other: On straining: prolapsing internal haemorrhoids at 3, 7 and 11 o’clock, reducible manually. DRE: no mass. Proctoscopy: grade III haemorrhoids.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Grade III internal haemorrhoids
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Grade III (Goligher) internal haemorrhoids with bleeding. Colonoscopy before haemorrhoid treatment (age 58, never investigated). Then rubber band ligation or haemorrhoidectomy.

mustInclude.note: ASCRS 2024 and NG12/DG56: rectal bleeding at 58 needs colonic evaluation (colonoscopy, or FIT-guided per local pathway) before it is attributed to haemorrhoids.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — management of hemorrhoids
guideline.section: Grade III: office procedures (rubber band ligation) or excisional haemorrhoidectomy; colonic evaluation when bleeding is not typical or the patient is at risk of colorectal neoplasia
guideline.citation: Hawkins AT, Davis BR, Bhama AR, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of hemorrhoids. Dis Colon Rectum. 2024;67:614–623.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — suspected cancer: recognition and referral (lower gastrointestinal tract cancers)
guideline.section: Lower GI: rectal bleeding at ≥ 50 on the colorectal pathway (FIT-first since 2023)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12). First published 2015; lower GI recommendations updated 2023 to incorporate DG56.

rationale: Base haemorrhoid case: Goligher grade III (prolapse requiring manual reduction). The safety check is that a 58-year-old with bleeding is sent for colonic evaluation before the haemorrhoids are blamed.
